scenes.heading: Running your first small ad budget test

sents.d: Running your first small ad budget test
Start small, test one variable, track cost per result.
Before committing a large budget to ads, run a small test — often $5–20 per day for a week or two — to learn what messaging and audience actually convert before scaling spend.

scenes.heading: Change one thing at a time

sents.d: Change only one variable at a time (the image, the headline, or the audience) so you know what caused a change in results, rather than changing everything at once and guessing why performance shifted.
Track cost per result (per lead, per sale, per click) rather than just total spend — a $500 campaign that generates 10 paying customers is far better than a $100 campaign that generates none.

take: Test ads with a small daily budget and judge by cost per result.
